rv.q: It’s easily my favourite musical of the year, and deserves a long life.
David Lindsay-Abaire’s Tony award-winning 2021 adaptation of his own 2001 play, with a gorgeous and utterly earwormy score by Jeanine Tesori, is a quirky, heartfelt delight.
Longhurst’s ebullient staging, like the musical itself, keeps wrongfooting you.
And in this, it is a clear success.
After a long drought, Hampstead has a hit.
Uplifting and achingly funny, the original New York production was the biggest winner of the 2023. Tony awards.
Yet somehow the evening sparkles.
Few manage to do so quite as sweetly and seemingly effortlessly as this genuinely delightful Broadway transfer penned by David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori.

Walking the few steps back to the Tube station, buoyed as only an unexpectedly perfect musical can buoy me, I wondered why anyone would spend an evening doomscrolling on their phone alone and scared, when they could spend that time in the company of Kimberly and her goofy friends and dodgy family.
No wonder that it won five Tonys, including Best Musical, when it appeared on Broadway in 2022 (after an off-Broadway run the previous year).
What an utterly charming gem this is.
Kimberly Akimbo is funny, touching and profound, a musical that celebrates life precisely because it understands how fragile it can be.
Instead, it mixes poignancy with silliness, finding humour in the absurdity of life while quietly reminding us that none of us has as much time as we think we have.
Plenty of audience members will enjoy its pleasant optimism and undemanding approach, but its big reputation and award-winning status deliver only disappointment.
This is an absolutely gorgeous production, with staging that is just stunning.
Kimberly Akimbo is what theatre should be, and I would encourage everyone to go and see it while it is still in London to experience something truly beautiful.
Kimberly Akimbo is an exceptionally entertaining evening out with exactly as much to give as you are emotionally able to take.
This comedy musical didn’t disappoint.
At its heart, Kimberly Akimbo is a reckoning with mortality, something that everyone faces.
It is an odd choice for a musical, but the result is something richly human and life-affirming, which shines as bright as Kimberly’s spirit.
Tesori’s show is fun, heartwarming and justifies its transfer to London’s Hampstead Theatre.
Kimberly Akimbo doesn't dig deeply into any of its themes: fraud, abuse, mortality and murder all get mentioned but jettisoned for another aside.
I think it's worth travelling to North West London to see this.
Kimberly Akimbo is a charming, quirky and beautifully realised production, packed with colourful characters and genuinely touching moments.

cn.t: Critics hail this Tony-winning musical as a quirky, heartfelt gem that defies expectations. Maria Friedman earns widespread praise in the lead role, while Tesori's score and the show's blend of humor with poignant themes win hearts.
